checks.check: No raw endpoint/options/source contents/credentials/refs/session capabilities enter wire replies, logs, prompts, receipts, telemetry, checkpoints or artifacts.
checks.evidence: removal-privacy-child.ts seeds 8 distinct canaries (endpoint/password/options/rows/secretRef/capability/sdk/journal) into a privateFailure error injected on SDK close, keychain, and fs read/write. Every manage()/call() reply is routed through safe(), which asserts the JSON text of each reply is <16384 bytes, contains none of the canaries, and never contains 'db:v2:'; it also pins any safeMessage to one of 3 fixed strings. The final wire check (`wire.includes(opened.sessionHandle)`/`capability`) confirms no session handle/capability leaks. The saved-scope half of the fixture additionally asserts the persisted receipt's keys are exactly ['cleanupRefs','outcome','requestMac','ticket'] with no canary inside. Both files' CM-S4-PRIVACY/NO-PERSIST subtests passed (ok 4 in session-driver-logs.test.ts TAP; ok 2 in composed-probe-logs.test.ts TAP).

checks.check: Temporary discard/state/retry performs zero registry/keychain/persistent-cache access; owner loss cannot recover temporary state.
checks.evidence: removal-privacy-child.ts mocks fsPromises.readFile/writeFile and the keystore getKey/setKey/deleteKey to throw and count calls, then drives the full remove/removalState/retryRemovalCleanup/status/session.end sequence on the temporary scope and asserts files===0 and keychain===0 before/after; it also asserts the on-disk state and root trees are byte-for-byte unchanged (tree() hash comparison). After `session.end`, the same ticket returns `session-expired`, and a brand-new session opened under a different connectionIdentity/epoch returns `invalid-input` for the same ticket, proving owner loss cannot recover the temporary removal state. The proof line `{"files":0,"keychain":0,"closes":2,...}` is emitted and asserted by removal-privacy-run.ts for both source and compiled modes.

checks.check: Errors are bounded fixed safe messages, including underlying SDK close and journal failures.
checks.evidence: The injected privateFailure throws on the first simulated driver close (closes counter, asserted ===2 total) and on keychain deleteKey during saved-scope credential-journal cleanup (fail=true). Every reply touching these paths goes through safe(), which asserts message/safeMessage equals one of 3 fixed strings ('The removal outcome is unknown...', 'The registration was removed. Application-owned cleanup is pending.', 'The registration was removed. Source data was preserved.', or 'Invalid connection request.') — never the raw canary-laden error. The saved-scope retryRemovalCleanup path is driven through a real pending->removed transition under journal failure with the same bounded-message check.

verdict.reason: Both named tests ('...hide SDK journal and capability canaries' and '...composed removal keeps temporary persistence poisoned and owner loss unrecoverable') pass and genuinely exercise the canary/poisoned-port privacy and no-persist contract via the new removal-privacy-child.ts/run.ts fixtures; all three acceptance checks are satisfied by code inspection plus the passing TAP output for those two cases. The daemon's file-level FAIL on composed-probe-logs.test.ts comes solely from the pre-existing, unrelated 'CM-S2-A9' sibling test failing on 'listen EINVAL' (a long tmp-socket-path limit documented as already-present in t19's evidence note, 'original 115-byte socket-path startup failure retained'); it is not one of this Task's named tests and this Task did not touch that test's code, so it does not bear on t20's own checks, though the daemon's overall exit-code-1 verdict will still fail the Task per the harness rule. — but the daemon's checks failed: tests.
